messages:
raj (SE): Hey team — customer (FinTech EU) pushed back on our default KMS approach in the questionnaire. They require HSM-backed CMKs and anti-key-escrow guarantees for EU-only keys. Asking if we can provide an exception/compensating controls for Redwood Private deployed in their VPC.

samantha (InfoSec): We don't have an HSM-backed KMS integrated in the Private product today. For hosted we use cloud KMS; Dedicated has customer-managed KMS option but not HSM-anchored by default.

ashwin (AE): Customer says HSM is a hard requirement per their procurement compliance. They're willing to accept compensating controls if we get approval. Timeline: POC in 2 weeks.

maria (Legal): @samantha can you list the compensating controls they'd need to accept risk? We'll need a short write-up for their vendor risk team.

samantha (InfoSec): Draft list I'm proposing: 1) Customer-managed KMS with keys provisioned in customer AWS account (no key material leaves customer account), 2) Dedicated VPC + private endpoints only, 3) Strict IAM separation + KMS access logs exported to customer S3 + retention 7 years, 4) Quarterly key rotation and attestation, 5) Proof of SOC2 + pen-test report, 6) Live remote attestation session with ops if needed.

raj (SE): To be explicit — in the Private POC we can run the KMS proxy in their account and use the customer's CMK for envelope encryption. Key material remains in their KMS (no export). That should mitigate 'key escrow' concerns.

maria (Legal): Sounds reasonable. We need wording: "Redwood will not store or export customer CMK material; all master keys remain under customer's control. Redwood will only hold ephemeral data keys encrypted with the customer's CMK." I can draft clause.

security-bot: Automated checklist created: /security-exception #12345 — includes required controls, evidence checklist, and review due in 7 days.

samantha (InfoSec): Two open items before we present to CISO: A) confirmation from infra that the Private deployment installer supports using a customer KMS proxy in their account (raj said yes but need ops sign-off), B) ops runbook for the attestation session + proof artifacts.

raj (SE): Ops confirmed in thread: installer supports external KMS endpoints (tested in internal staging). I'll attach the install snippet to the vendor package. snippet: ```yaml kms: endpoint: "https://kms.customer-eu.aws" use_envelope: true```. 

ciso: Reviewed proposed compensating controls. Risk acceptance granted contingent on: 1) Legal clause signed, 2) ops attestation run and logs forwarded to customer, 3) SOC2 and latest penetration test evidence uploaded to vendor portal. If all three met, I sign off. :thumbsup:

maria (Legal): I'll prepare the clause and queue for e-sign. Raj — please attach the attestation runbook and the installer snippet to the ticket. Samantha, can you own verifying SOC2/pentest docs are current?

samantha (InfoSec): On it — will verify and upload by EOD tomorrow.

ashwin (AE): Great — I'll update the customer: we can meet their requirement via customer-managed KMS + the listed compensating controls; CISO conditional approval in place. Will ask for their timeline to provide SOC2/pentest.

security-bot: #12345 status updated: awaiting evidence (SOC2, pentest), awaiting signed legal clause, awaiting ops attestation. Due: 1763570000.

raj (SE): Quick note for the POC: suggest enabling verbose KMS logging and configuring S3 notifications so customer can trigger alerts on any KMS Deny events during the POC window. That gives them live proof keys never leave account.

maria (Legal): Thanks everyone. I'll file the clause draft in the ticket and ping when ready.

ashwin (AE): Thanks team — will sync with customer and loop back here. :pray:
